## Unreleased

- F239-221-1: Replace diagnostic log correlation of source clocks with native monotonic clock reads before and after the successful observer-start command. Red: the unchanged owner requires a logged native request and fails without a clock bracket. Green: the shared collection source-frame and trace cases pass 12/12, four HWP layout cases pass, and the Browser, Editor and Terminal descriptor cases pass. The collector preserves the raw clock receipts and same-session host/PID/window/surface identity, removes the event-log argument parser, and keeps the declared source precision and measurement thresholds. Application acceptance remains under F212.14-5-5.

- F239-221: Map each view document source-frame clock to native monotonic time from the successful `frames.start` result and matching native request/reply. Red: the unchanged mapper combines the view clock with main-page event-batcher timestamps and misses a capture that starts after its source frame; the cadence evaluator also counts 8,976 ms of observer idle time outside a gesture whose boundary portion is at most 9 ms. Green: the collection owner passes 27/27, the window metric evaluator passes 21/21, all four plugin consumer owner cases pass, and the four focused drag-cadence cases pass. Ambiguous intervals remain preserved; one-shot selection requires a guaranteed post-request frame, and drag cadence charges only possible boundary overlap inside the gesture. `make docs-check` passes. Application acceptance remains under F212.14-5-5.

- F239-223-1: Trace native-clock admission, UI entry and closure return at existing sync/present boundaries on both hosts. Keep dispatch order unchanged and skip clock reads and label construction while tracing is disabled. Both owning wrappers pass after assertion Reds; generated event classes and their four owners pass. This adds diagnostic evidence and does not establish a cadence correction.

- F239-219: Await expected AppKit reference text after each asynchronous key dispatch. `wait-document` uses text notifications and accepts matching intermediate text with marked composition; final `wait` still requires unmarked text. Native Red/Green covers marked text and missing-document errors; both host parsers accept the action after tracked Reds, and their focused owner tests pass. The approved readiness activation explicitly selects Korean 2-Set, produces ㅎ, and restores the original input source and frontmost application. Run 34's immediate snapshot does not prove a routing defect. The first activation attempt read its asynchronous callback too early; the corrected target waits for it. The deferred consumer case is post-change Green only, has a per-test timeout and verifies close. The retained activation log includes the OS IMK mach-port diagnostic `error messaging the mach port for IMKCFRunLoopWakeUpReliable` despite passing assertions; it is not evidence about input routing.

- F239-190: Correct the historical attribution of the capture summary assertion. The earlier summary-predicate failures are recorded under F239-78, whose startup-delay cause remains open. This corrects the record only and makes no product-fix or not-reproduced claim.

The owning parser Red reproduces that assertion failure; the same test and all 8 parser tests pass with the corrected matcher. `make host-parity-check` and `make docs-check` pass.

- F239-47-34: Correct the ScreenCaptureKit stop comment.
  `minimumFrameInterval` limits the requested update rate and does not guarantee
  idle callbacks at that cadence. Stop waits for a callback at or beyond the
  requested display boundary and reports an explicit error when its existing
  one-second wait
  expires. Capture behavior and the 33 ms criterion are unchanged.

- F212.10-core-3-9: Correlate terminal reload replies with native post
  acceptance. Start from the host dispatch record and join its exact target
  tuple and outcome to the declared-plugin page receipt/reply. Reject stale,
  missing and duplicate dispatch evidence; ignore page-call arguments and
  cross-layer timestamps. The owner test passes 1/1 and the exported structural
  source audit passes for all three changed e2e files. The two-host runtime
  result is recorded under F212.10-core-3-10; primary `make e2e-check` passes,
  while the full window suite was not run.

- F212.10-core-3-8: Verify that a main-page reload receives a current-generation
  terminal view call whose reply is accepted by the host's native post API.
  Preserve the current-page event evidence, terminal session ID and shell
  continuation checks. The focused consumer test passes 1/1 and the exact
  Wails/Tauri reload case passes 2/2. Runtime tuple and artifact details are
  recorded under F212.10-core-3-10. F212.10-core-3-2 remains open because this
  case does not verify every host view call has a matching page receipt.

- F239-47-33: Add approval-gated e2e selectors for F8-9 gksrmf and F143 gksk
  input sequences plus ten project
  close/reopen lifecycle cycles per host using the previously approved
  eight-vowel gesture. The cases are defined but have not been run. The
  separate P87 runtime recorded under F239-47-32 did not execute these
  selectors or any close/reopen cycle. F143 now sends
  Enter to both the AppKit reference and terminal; the reference must end with
  a newline, while the terminal checks its pre-Enter text and shell output.
  The lifecycle selector reads native input actions from validated transaction
  envelopes, compares committed screen cells plus current marked text with the
  AppKit document, preserves the full gesture capture, and performs two
  project close/reopen passes. It makes no overlay-operation claim.

- F239-47-30-1: Report the AppKit window color space through a one-shot
  diagnostic method. The query returns its localized name and the SHA-256
  fingerprint of ICC profile data when available, without changing the
  window. Before the change, both host declaration tests failed because the
  method was absent. The Wails and Tauri declaration tests and the native
  `window_facts_test` pass; `cargo fmt --check -p soksak-host-tauriv2` and
  `make docs-check` pass. One non-activating check against stable 0.0.21 macOS
  arm64 Wails and Tauri bundles validates the exact response shape, missing
  window error and unchanged stable `host.window` facts without pinning the OS
  color profile. Both host error audits pass, and the test processes end with
  their endpoints removed. After requiring a string ICC hash before the digest
  pattern, the same two-host case passes again with empty error audits and the
  same cleanup results.

- F239-47-32: Give image regions a marked-buffer-only input client. The
  accumulated `NSTextView` document exposed unmarked committed text as
  preedit. The region now implements `NSTextInputClient` on `NSView` with a
  local UTF-16 marked buffer, validated replacement and substring queries,
  ordered commit boundaries, and no terminal-history context. Closing commits
  pending text once, detaches the responder, discards marked state, and
  releases the diagnostic context override. Red reproduces the retained-suffix
  report and, with pending commit disabled, fails close-commit and teardown
  assertions. An ordinary `NSTextView` reference confirms that `NSNotFound`
  replaces the current marked composition, and the four-key vowel document
  matches the reference at every key. Green: the focused input-transaction,
  Hangul, and basic region owners pass 3/3. On the marked-buffer candidate
  runtime from the P87 cohort (macOS 26.6.2 arm64; core and Wails/Tauri hosts
  0.0.21, terminal 0.0.21, VT 0.0.17; staged `image_region.m` SHA-256
  `63894214c9d9038d97cdb9e342c6cc6952a77c542375cea55662b3a872637f3e`), both
  hosts matched all eight k, Backspace and Space document checkpoints to the
  same-window AppKit reference. Capture pixel samples showed caret movement
  from cell 14 to 16 during k4 and 24 to 22 during Backspace. Both
  full-gesture checks failed the unchanged 33 ms capture-gap limit: Wails
  33.755542 ms and Tauri 34.232958 ms. The read-only projection of preserved
  traces summarizes these samples and is not an independent acceptance result.
  This run did not test F143 gksk resyllabification or pass visual acceptance.
  Korean OS resyllabification and the historical WebKit close-cycle remain
  open under F239-47-32 and F239-47-33. The partial run is not acceptance.

- F239-47-31: Keep the original key-start offset for terminal status samples.
  A cursor notification arriving after the screen notification could make the
  observer recalculate the stage offset and exclude that screen event. The
  observer now retains both notifications through every reread. Red reproduces
  the screen-then-cursor interleave; the focused stage-window, coherent-reread
  and in-sample notification tests pass 3/3. Status and frame checks are
  unchanged.

- F212.10-core-3-7: Pair view call diagnostics by their native source generation.
  A reply from a recreated view could otherwise settle a call with the same id
  from an ended generation. The Workbench records generation on view call,
  reply and valid-source cancellation events; window-check pairs them by page,
  plugin, surface, generation and id. The focused Workbench tests pass 3/3,
  window-check tests pass 4/4, and `make events-check` and `make docs-check`
  pass. Runtime reload acceptance remains under F212.10-core-3-2.

- F239-37-3: Focus the selected Files tree label before sending Enter.
  Attempt03 showed the editor disabled and the selected node's declared
  `files.open` action, but the failure row did not appear. The owning helper
  test reproduced Enter running without a `core.focus` precondition. A shared
  declared-sidebar helper resolves the addressed control's unique index within
  its section, focuses it through `core.focus.set`, and waits for the exact
  focus status; the existing Enter route and failure-row assertions remain.
  The helper tests pass 9/9. The exact failure-row case passes on Wails and
  Tauri in the P47 local candidate cohort; the full runtime evidence is in
  `docs/features.md`.

- F239-51-1: Verify the corrected Files tree-node lookup in the actual window
  consumer. The focused failure-row case passes on Wails and Tauri after the

- F239-47-30: Record focused color-path experiments without changing the
  exact pixel criterion. In a non-activating WKWebView comparison, explicit
  sRGB window backing changed the captured Display P3 red and green samples
  while neutral gray stayed unchanged. A same-source 16-bit-float image
  assigned to the image-region layer converted back to the exact 12,288-byte
  BGRA8 source, but its ScreenCaptureKit crop still differed at 1,821 pixels.
  Under the native-surfaces capture contract, these unmatched results are

- F239-47-28: Reject a replacement at `committedLength` before AppKit.
  The previous path let AppKit replace
  committed `가` with `invalid`, then reported an out-of-range marked-text
  error after mutation. The callback now reports the committed-prefix error,
  preserves the document and last valid preedit, and latches later callbacks
  in the same scope. The controlled exported-region Red/Green case passes.

- F239-47-27: Accept the native focus action in input transactions and keep
  focus-only reports from acknowledging a key through retained preedit. The
  focused consumer tests pass 5/5; syntax, `make e2e-check`, and
  `make docs-check` pass. No activation or application run was made.

- F239-47-26: Read the current atomic native-input transactions in the IME
  acceptance consumer. Validate every action and error, require one CID, and
  match ordered native reports to exact terminal requests. The focused
  consumer tests pass 6/6; syntax, `make e2e-check`, and `make docs-check`
  pass. Activation checks were not run.

- F239-55: Require both nonempty run metadata values before the E2E runner
  probes the frontmost application or starts a child. The runner preserves

- F239-47-25: Publish native input callbacks as one transaction per outer
  scope. The fourth Korean vowel previously emitted a committed insert with
  a two-unit intermediate preedit, then a second report with the final
  three-unit marked text. The region now sends ordered insert, key, command
  and focus actions with one final strict preedit snapshot and separate
  callback errors. Responder changes, input-source changes and close commits
  use the same boundary; a committed-range replacement error stops before
  mutating the native document and rejects later callbacks in that scope with
  an unchanged-state record. A new scope clears the failure latch. Diagnostic
  input-context injection is absent from non-diagnostic builds, and AppKit
  remains the default context. Red and Green are recorded in F239-47-25. The
  transaction, Hangul, decoration and image-region native tests pass. Live
  Wails/Tauri acceptance remains open in F239-47-6.

- F239-37-3: Require the reloaded page to report the editor disabled before
  testing the Files failure row. The retained Wails and Tauri runs timed out
  with no failure row, while both installed editor manifests declare `*`;
  they do not record whether the editor was loaded or the Enter target had
  focus. The check now verifies the disabled plugin state, requires the
  selected node's declared `files.open` target and exact path parameters, and

- F239-53: Make high-level window-check clicks wait for `host.buttons` to
  report mask 0 before the press and again before the release. The P85 Files
  run received native 1007 refusals while another application was frontmost;

  pass, and the retained window run was not repeated.

- F239-52-2: Match `core.sidebars.source.id` with `core.plugin.snapshots`.
  The chosen plugin-host source uses `plugin:<plugin id>` while snapshot rows
  use the bare plugin id. Red: the retained two-host run had current Files
  snapshot rows but timed out because the helper compared `plugin:files` with
  `files`. The consumer now validates the source id against the status owner,

  `make e2e-check` passes after merging into the dependency-complete primary

- F239-47-2: Enable the declared `input:info` native callback records in the exact eight-vowel activation fixture. The previous P85 Tauri policy logged input only at `error`, which omitted `native.input.callback` records declared at `info`. The fixture now saves bounded key and callback records before evaluating the strict capture-gap result. No activation rerun or product fix is claimed; F239-47-6 remains open.

- F239-47-6/F239-47-10: Record the P85 two-host IME attempt. Both fixed AppKit reference sequences and all ten terminal documents matched. Tauri recorded a 34.660750 ms frame gap and Wails 33.694458 ms, exceeding the unchanged 33 ms limit; visual acceptance remains open. Metadata assigns all vowels the same foreground/background and underlines only the last marked vowel. The callback DTO does not expose AppKit selector names or `committedLength`. A second query replaced the original baseline, and the final frontmost observation conflicts with the runner's restore log; F239-47-24 tracks a valid session baseline. Both hosts and sidecars exited. Structured JSONL logs had zero error-level records, but both native host stderr logs contained `error messaging the mach port for IMKCFRunLoopWakeUpReliable`; the messages remain unclassified, with no established link to the capture gaps.

- F239-47-6: Record a blue underline observed beneath `preedit` in the terminal prompt path on a fresh Wails window. The corresponding terminal base cells had no underline, inverse or link flag, while `terminal.cursor.preedit` held `ㅏㅏㅏ`. Capture began after the mark was already present; its three non-activating frames produced no source raster or candidates and recorded no source drops. The painter remains unknown and visual acceptance remains open.
- F239-47-23: Keep the native image-region input document visually
  transparent while preserving AppKit composition state. The unchanged owning
  offscreen test measured 78 blue underline pixels for attributed `ㅏ` and 162
  for `ㅏㅏ`; the same frames retained the composition reports and a known-color
  sidecar IOSurface. The offscreen composite showed its green sentinel at the
  mapped image-layer center. AppKit converted source DeviceRGB `#20c020` into
  `(0.417, 0.773, 0.318)` in the `NSCalibratedRGBColorSpace` cache, so the test
  checks the documented green-channel separation after conversion. The focused
  test passes after `drawRect:` stops TextKit drawing, with zero underline
  pixels, committed text and marked ranges, and the composited sidecar layer
  intact. No activation or OS input method was used. P85 reported
  `attributed:false`, so the actual moving blue paint remains uncorrelated;
  live two-host visual acceptance remains under F239-47-6.

- F212.10-core-3-6: Retire a view's exposure registrations in the same
  synchronous workbench transition that accepts its exact source-generation
  end. Source retirement precedes `view-process-ended`, so the previous
  registration could remain selectable after its generation disappeared.
  The view lifecycle test fails before the correction at that interval and
  passes with a registration observer seeing the retired state. A delayed old
  end leaves a replacement registration intact. The focused view lifecycle and
  chooser guard tests pass 1/1 each; `source-origins.test.mjs` passes 5/5, and
  `make docs-check` passes. The preserved Wails application error has not been
  rechecked against this source change.

- F239-51: Import the Files tree lookup from its owning helper after extraction.

- F239-51-1: Track runtime acceptance of the tree lookup correction separately.
  The pre-correction two-host attempt is Red evidence; no post-correction window

- F239-52: Use `status.get` for plugin-host-only Files snapshots in the

- F239-52-1: Publish metadata-only snapshot sequences after native ACK acceptance
  and expose them through `core.plugin.snapshots`, including when no section is
  mounted. Source replacement and end remove exact-generation rows; undeclared

  The controlled ingress tests pass with delayed ACK and generation replacement.
  The project-close consumer subscribes for a newer matching source sequence,
  pulls `status.get`, and waits for a later accepted sequence when the value is
  stale. The focused consumer, ingress and plugin-process checks pass 33/33.

- F239-47-22: Clarify that a provider's presentation caret is runtime state
  outside the generic screen projection and replay hash. The owning projection

- F239-50-1: Keep an unrelated foreground application untouched, but reject a check result when cleanup cannot verify the shared session baseline. The unchanged cleanup accepted PID 30 while baseline PID 10 was expected; the owning test now requires explicit failure without activation.

- F239-50: Capture one frontmost `{pid, name, bundle}` identity for a window-check session and pass it to global setup and every isolated test worker. Reject missing, malformed, stale and tested-host baselines before a check; consume the shared identity in app cleanup instead of recapturing per process. The owning controlled worker and frontmost tests pass 18/18; the Node runner test passes 12/12. `make e2e-check` and `make docs-check` pass. No application was launched or activated.

- F212.10-core-3-5: Remove a view's exposure registrations when its current
  native process ends. The registration belongs to that process, so keeping it
  while its generation is absent lets source selection choose an ended view.
  The owning lifecycle test fails before the correction because the ended view
  remains registered, then passes with replacement registration and delayed-old-
  end coverage. The new case and existing view restart/subscription cleanup
  case pass 2/2; `make docs-check` and `make exposure-check` pass. `make
  boundaries` remains blocked by the unchanged `e2e/browser-cohort-upgrade.test.mjs`
  references to sidecar package names. No GUI or full suite was run.

- F239-37-9: Start the existing Files project-close check by opening its
  disposable project before waiting for mounted sidebar sections. The project
  library has no plane, so `core.sidebars` correctly reports no drawn sections
  there. After close, the check now verifies newer declared tree and bookmark
  snapshots with exact no-project values, no stale rows, no application error,
  and no Files sections drawn in the library. Red: the prior Wails check timed
  out on `core.sidebars: []` before opening the test project. Green: the exact
  project-close case passes on Wails (2.419 s) and Tauri (2.095 s), 2/2. Both
  log audits report no error records, process waits confirm both hosts and all
  four sidecars ended, and endpoint scans are empty. The result validates this
  named check only; it does not claim the full Files suite or a public release.

- F239-37: All nine separately tracked Files window checks for the current
  plugin-host snapshot contract are complete. This closes only those named
  checks and does not claim full Files-suite or public-release acceptance.

- F239-37-8: Wait for the current Files tree source to accept a declared UI
  snapshot before using its sequence as a baseline. A source change may leave
  the section cleared with a pending subscription and a null `acceptedSeq`.
  The helper now waits for a current source, a ready subscription, a mounted
  section and an integer accepted sequence, and includes the last observed
  `core.sidebars` payload on failure. The unchanged consumer test reproduced
  immediate refusal of the pending state; the focused consumer tests pass
  4/4. No producer or status contract changed.
- F239-48-5-1: Discover test owners from tracked package manifests, including
  the root e2e package, before checking cross-package path reads. Red: the
  production owner list omitted `e2e`; the owning test failed on the actual

  components, but that exception does not permit implementation-path reads.

- F239-48-5: Exclude only declared application window checks from the core
  package-name boundary audit. Classification requires an `e2e/` test source,
  an import of `open` from `@soksak/window-check/app.mjs`, and a call through
  that imported binding. Red: the unchanged audit reported the Files and VT
  sidecar names in the browser cohort window check. Green: the focused owner
  test passes 1/1 and `make boundaries` passes for 16 components. Regular core
   tests still reject plugin names, and implementation-path reads remain checked.

- F239-47-20: Wait for each coherent terminal document to match the same-window
  AppKit reference after input receipt. Backspace can first clear the preedit
  while the PTY still shows eight committed vowels, then publish the expected
  seven-vowel screen in a later status event. The caller now waits on the
  existing event stream within the unchanged 1500 ms deadline and preserves
  every intermediate status and capture frame. The delayed-status owner test
  reproduces the old first-coherent result and passes with the completion
  predicate; `terminal-ime-document.test.mjs` passes 23/23, `make e2e-check`,
  `make docs-check`, syntax checks, and `git diff --check` pass. No application
  run was made; F239-47-6 acceptance remains open.

- F212.12-2-2-4-8-2-4: Stream each accepted image source raster to the
  diagnostic artifact writer before matching-history eviction. Keep matching
  history at 64 MiB and 512 snapshots, and bound queued plus active raster
  bytes independently at 64 MiB. Remove the aggregate artifact byte limit;
  retain the 512-identity limit and report pending-budget overflow explicitly.
  Manifest format 2 records history bytes, pending bytes, and total artifact
  bytes separately. Red: unchanged `capture_metadata_test` failed because the
  former aggregate artifact limit prevented 20 unique 3,520,512-byte rasters
  from all being saved. Green: the same test passes 1/1, including a blocked
  writer accepting 19 rasters and explicitly rejecting the 20th; the matcher
  test passes 1/1, visual-capture manifest tests pass 12/12, native build and
  `make docs-check` pass. No live capture or activation was run.

- F239-47-21: Attach the resulting composition snapshot to each committed
  native insert so committed bytes and retained preedit arrive atomically. Keep
  composition-only updates on the compose event. The non-activating owning native
  test passes for partial commits, unchanged preedit, and commit-before-Backspace.

- F239-37-3: Give the file-open failure window check its own 120-second
  timeout. This annotation change does not claim a new test or runtime result.
- F262-6: Extend the existing project-close window check to require mounted

- F239-47-19: Plan visual stages against the exact cursor/render overlay frame
  while preserving the earlier screen rows as their source. The base screen
  sequence may precede the overlay sequence when rows-only status deduplication

  The owning visual-capture tests pass 12/12; `node --check
  e2e/activation/ime.test.mjs`, `make e2e-check`, and `make docs-check` pass.
  No activation rerun was performed; F239-47-6 acceptance remains open.
  The stage planner consumes the caller's top-level `presented` field. It uses

  The caller-shaped test reproduced the previous nonexistent `region` lookup;
  the corrected frame-planning/watermark cases pass 2/2.
  The activation check appends each raw observer callback to

- F239-37-3: Migrate the file-open failure check from removed `files.selection`
  and `files.open` status waits to the declared `files.tree` snapshot. The check

- F239-47-18: Use the coherent current reread for a terminal input observation.
  A transient first compose/cursor read can be stale even when the subsequent
  reread matches current watched events and the presented screen. The activation
  caller now selects one coherent snapshot and uses its compose, cursor, screen,
  region and event slice for the saved observation and final assertion. Red:
  the owning selector test returned the stale empty first pair and prior event
  slice instead of a coherent `ㅏ` reread. Green: the focused owning cases pass
  2/2; the activation source syntax check, `git diff --check` and `make
  docs-check` pass. Key receipts, frame/render/source checks, visual measurement
  and the 33 ms frame-gap limit are unchanged. No activation rerun was made;
  F239-47-6 acceptance remains open.
- F238-c-18: Record terminal current-source view-literal validation as complete. Keep the pinned SDK release and owner-pin requirement under F238-c-11-1.

- F238-c-20: Record existing current-source plugin checks by owner and correct the plugin check matrix. No source implementation or public SDK release is included.

- F212.10-core-3-3: Defer an unmounted view during undrawn preparation
  without inventing native geometry. The plane creates and mounts a new view
  during drawing, after preparation has begun. Red: the unchanged host
  placement test started composition readiness before that mount and failed;
  a held-disposal fixture also showed that the old disposed entry could satisfy
  a composition wait without a replacement.
  Green: preparation reports the deferred view ID separately from actual
  placements; the compositor excludes it from applied and predicted geometry,
  and the drawn commit waits for mount registration and composition readiness.
  A disposed entry cannot satisfy the wait before its replacement registers.
  Placement results reject missing, extra, duplicate and invalid deferred IDs.
  A disposed drawn view rejects through the caller without leaving an
  unhandled preparation promise. The focused host, remount-composition,
  compositor, native-paint and no-bridge tests pass (4/4, 1/1, 4/4, 8/8 and
  4/4). Runtime revalidation is pending; the host wire format is unchanged.
- F212.10-core-3-4: Validate full host placement replies before projecting the
  result onto the current compositor record. The workbench sends retained
  dormant tabs with the active record, so an undrawn host reply can defer an ID
  absent from that record. Red: the unchanged compositor test fails with
  `surface placement cannot defer tab-c2zkow` for the exact full-request shape.
  Green: the same case validates the full ID partition, projects only current
  record IDs, and keeps a dormant-only reply out of an empty record. It rejects
  omitted current IDs, duplicate requests, missing, extra and duplicate reply
  IDs, unrequested deferrals, unsupported plugins, non-view compositions and
  drawn deferrals. The focused owning case passes 1/1 in 88.8 ms. The host wire
  format is unchanged. The ba6 failure also exposed that an undrawn record can
  precede its active tab: the retained request now omits that tab until its
  drawn record. Mounted dormant views stay in the request; an absent background
  view stays with its background session; a loaded hidden view without a
  background declaration mounts in a hidden workbench slot before placement.
  Red: the initial drawn placement used `memorySaver.place` before project tab
  state initialized and sent a cold unload-declared view to the host. Green: an
  undrawn preparation skips cold hidden views without waiting, while a drawn
  placement waits for startup classification; enabled memory saver excludes a
  tab that starts unloaded, and disabled memory saver mounts the loaded hidden
  view. Readiness rejection settles every waiting placement. A failed tab-state open
  now rejects drawn placement while the existing tried signal still resolves.
  Red: the old tried-signal race let two placement waiters proceed after the
  open failed; Green: the open-result gate rejects both before observation or
  memory-saver placement. The actual host barrier and startup tests pass 4/4,
  the project readiness test passes 2/2, and the focused compositor case passes
  1/1. An additional Red in `surface-view.test.mjs` showed that a cold retained
  view outside the current plane had no initial scale and its first
  `runtime.textSize.read` returned `surface fixture-retained-text-size-tab is not
  in the layout`. Green uses the retained tab's owning card factor multiplied by
  the current frame factor; the actual view-call returns 1.875 for factors 1.5
  and 1.25. The workbench-only resolver is removed before the host placement
  request. A mounted dormant view continues to retain its last scale, while a

Red: unchanged validation accepted a blink-off cursor with a rectangle and color. Green: the owning metadata test rejects stale values for blink-off and hidden cursors while retaining valid null metadata and drawn cursor cases; `terminal-ime-visual.test.mjs` passes 10/10.

- F239-45: Tauri view callbacks carry a local origin registered before native document creation. Closing, replacing or removing a view retires that origin before resource release; message, navigation-state, process-end and responsiveness callbacks from stale origins cannot affect the current view channel. Stale callbacks write `host.trace.view.callback-cancelled` when performance tracing is enabled, while a producer `view.error` retains its captured plugin and surface. The controlled origin tests pass 7/7, including malformed and native error envelopes; existing view error and view call record tests pass 1/1 each. The host test targets compile, and `cargo fmt --check`, `make docs-check`, `make boundaries` and `make events-check` pass. `make parity-check` reports four existing findings: the missing F266 feature link, stale bilingual examples parity counts and the unclaimed Wails starter test. The application shutdown matrix remains pending under F239-26-2.
- F239-46: Plugin-host and view source instances use a window-wide JavaScript-safe generation. The main page installs and buffers lifecycle and snapshot listeners before atomically seeding the active origins and issued-generation floor; delayed registration and end events cannot restore or remove an older source. Snapshot delivery waits for native acceptance and rechecks the exact source and recipient, while pull and expanded requests carry internal generation metadata and stale requests return an explicit cancellation. Red: controlled tests exposed an old queued registration after same-plugin recreation, a stale snapshot routed to a replacement recipient, a view call from generation 1 reaching the generation 2 command layer, and a startup-floor registration that could create a ghost source. A controlled Wails replacement during an old reply verifies that generation-scoped cleanup preserves a reused call ID. A delayed old host-end removes only its generation's exposure registrations and preserves the replacement layer and sessions. Native lifecycle ordering supports the global floor across plugin-host and view sources: both hosts serialize source changes on the window main thread and deliver lifecycle events in emission order. Green: the Workbench declared-source, source-origin, declared-section, sidebar, plugin-host-call, view-command and surface-view tests pass; the Wails plugin-host, source-origin, view-call and restart-order tests pass 48/48; Tauri origin and stale-ACK/pull tests pass. The plugin producer and public `sok-view` snapshot messages are unchanged. `make docs-check`, `make boundaries`, `make exposure-check`, and `make events-check` pass. `make parity-check` reports four unrelated findings: F266 classification, bilingual examples counts, and the unclaimed Wails starter test. The named Files project-folder/bookmark runtime case passed on both hosts; remaining Files runtime checks stay under F239-37.
- F239-49: Tauri routes source lifecycle, snapshot, call, reply, end and responsiveness events through one ordered main-page `Channel`; startup installs it before querying source origins, page reload retires it, and send failures are returned. Wails keeps its FIFO transport. Both hosts tag `view-responsiveness` with the producing generation, and the workbench applies only current-generation notices while recording stale notices. Red: the unchanged Tauri runtime and stream tests lacked the shared channel/allowlist behavior; the unchanged workbench accepted a delayed generation 1 notice after generation 2 replaced the same surface; the unchanged Wails payload omitted `generation`. Green: runtime stream tests pass 12/12, Tauri stream tests pass 8/8, current/retired responsiveness callback tests pass, Workbench consumer tests pass, and the Wails producer test passes. `view-presentation-abandoned` remains on its existing path because it records completed presentation-wait loss rather than live view state. `make docs-check`, `make boundaries`, `make exposure-check`, and `make events-check` pass. `make parity-check` retains four existing findings: the F266 link, bilingual examples counts, and the unclaimed Wails starter test. Package tests do not establish full application runtime acceptance.

- F212.12-2-2-4: The approved two-host reference and terminal input checks passed, and Wails met the capture bound. Tauri input also produced the expected reference text and terminal output, but its terminal recording exceeded 33 ms by 0.1167917 ms between consecutive complete frames. The callback trace records no intervening frame and no writer rejection. With mach timebase 125/3, the display delta is 794803 ticks, arrival delta 797653 ticks, and synchronous processing spans 33066 and 45061 ticks. Processing completion precedes asynchronous compression and file writing, so these measurements do not cover writer I/O. The raw capture and runner output remain available for diagnosis; no cause is assigned. The input method and original frontmost application were restored. F212.12-2-2-4-8 tracks display-cadence investigation.

- F212.12-2-2-4-7: Capture now checks Core Video pixel-buffer lock and unlock results. A failed lock reports its frame and `CVReturn`, avoids base-address access and unlock, and releases the pending-writer permit. A failed unlock reports its result, rejects and frees the copied frame, and releases the permit without submitting a write. The owning `capture_metadata_test` reproduces both unchecked-result failures on the old path and passes after the correction; `make docs-check` passes on macOS 26.6.2 arm64.

- F212.12-2-2-4-8-1: A non-activating native control renders seven distinct Metal pixel IDs and records each drawable's actual presentation time; ScreenCaptureKit captures the same IDs from the window. The first unpaced attempt skipped five drawables (`presentedTime == 0`) and remains incomplete evidence. An intermediate assertion incorrectly treated a repeated captured ID 0 as a second drawable; the test now retains every sample and allows repeated IDs in nondecreasing order. The final detailed event-paced measurement observed all seven presentation and unique capture IDs: the largest Metal interval was 24.999875 ms and the largest ScreenCaptureKit `displayTime` interval was 26.457542 ms. With timebase 125/3, captured times for matching IDs were 10.01125–13.7735 ms earlier than Metal `presentedTime`. The APIs report separate observations and do not promise timestamp equality or ordering; the test compares each stream's cadence and reports the signed offset. The final source's single-test runner passes 1/1 (0.836 s); a separate detailed measurement passes in 353.2 ms; and `make docs-check` passes on macOS 26.6.2 arm64. These executions remain distinct. This controlled Metal path does not identify the Tauri/WebKit gap; F212.12-2-2-4-8 remains open.

- F262-8: An origin ends only when its tab leaves the stored layout of its own space. The display of another space no longer drops the origins of the tabs of the spaces that are not displayed, which caused the refusal `tab X has no origin`.

- F244-2: `make declared-ui-benchmark` measures a fully expanded 5000-node tree within 16 levels and a 1000-item command list in separate supervised processes, keeping the 2000 ms and 500 ms acceptance bounds. Each JSON measurement records complete drawing and binding counts, elapsed time, outcome, package and runtime versions, platform and load. Invalid timing, missing drawing or binding work, and exceeded bounds fail. The 10 benchmark tests have Red and Green evidence, and both existing full-size drawing tests pass. Workbench 0.0.20 on darwin arm64 25.6.0, Node 26.11.1 and jsdom 30.0.1 measured 327.2 ms for the tree and 81.0 ms for the list at load average 10.99. Documentation, parity and boundary checks pass.

- F262-7: The presentation refusal of a view tab without an origin names the tab, its plugin, its space and project, the path that created the tab, and whether this session recorded its origin. Each tab creation site names its path.
- F212.12-2-1: A view accepts the first mouse down of an inactive window, so the press reaches the page of the view and the view becomes the first responder. Before, AppKit consumed that press for the activation of the window, so a click on a view card gave the view no keyboard focus. A document region keeps the refusal. Red: `view_focus_test` failed both the page press and the first responder assertions on the unchanged source; Green after the change, three consecutive runs.
- F262-6a: The view bridge serves `runtime.project(listener)`, which gives the listener the last project of the plugin host at once and makes no call to the host, as `runtime.theme` does. A plugin host page that subscribed the project message through `runtime.native.on` was refused by the host.
- F262-4a: A layout write names its writing path (add space, saved layout, recreate or library replacement), and each view tab that it stores without an origin member is recorded in the application log with its tab, plugin and path.

- F262-3: The project settings file is written in the current numbered form by both hosts: a settings write migrates the file at its entry and stores the `format` member, and the diagnostics fixture writes the current form too.
- F262: The projects check reads the project settings file in its current numbered form, and a tab of a new space keeps its origin until a stored layout has held it and dropped it, so the first tab of an added space no longer fails to present with `has no origin`.

- F212.12-1-10-6: The view import map has one owner. The host inserts the import map of the core it runs directly after the doctype of each view page, so a view page holds no import map of its own. The host records each exposure request, reply and unmatched reply with the id and where the relay holds it.

- F212.6a-1-3-2-2: The page-close stall cause is identified: the pthread mutex of `CFRunLoopWakeUp` is the main run loop's `_lock`, held in short repeated stretches by the main thread itself while it runs the WebKit page-close work; a background waiter queues behind it, and the circular wait with the IPC receive queue stretches the stall. The cause is not host code, so no code changes.

- F218-1: The Rust host installs the panic hook as the first action of the process, so a `host.panic` raised before the writer exists stays in the start buffer and is stored when the writer opens. The thread that ends the process after a panic waits up to 5 s for the writer; without an attached writer in that time, the process ends with status 101 and writes the record with its stack on the standard error. The Go goroutine entrance waits for the writer the same way (docs/spec/hosts.md#process-lifecycle, contract `log.panic.before-writer-is-stored-when-the-writer-opens`).

Tests: `project_removal_test.rs` (two) and `notifications_test.rs` (one) failed before the change and pass after it. The census rule `rs.lock-result` (in `packages/plugin-api/census-rules.json`) lists each `lock()`, `read()` and `write()` result that is matched, mapped or unwrapped; it is pending on F218-2.5 with 221 findings, which the remaining groups of F218-2 convert.

Any other path, a requester that is not enabled, and a path that no grant names are not found, and each writes `error: core root: <path> is not granted to <plugin>`. It posts the ready message `{event: "view.ready", plugin, document}` through the `sok-view` handler at start, keeps each host message whose event source is the window and that carries `sok: 1` in a queue of 256, and exposes one global, `window.sokView`, whose `attach` delivers the queued and later messages in order. A message that fails a check, and a 257th queued message, is reported through the handler as `error: view channel: <reason> for <plugin>` and dropped. `packages/plugin-api/view.js` (`@soksak/plugin-api/view`) `createViewChannel({handler})` sends through the handler and reads host messages through `window.sokView.attach`, and `createViewBridge({handler, report})` runs `createCalls` and `createSnapshotSender` over the channel. `index.js` exports `VIEW_IMPORTS`, the four entries of the view import map. - F212.5-3: `sok` in Go and Rust computes the granted items of a requester (`GrantedFiles` and `granted_files`, host contract case `install.granted-items`). The result holds the `/modules/<package>/<module>` file of each item that another enabled plugin contributes to a point of the requester, and the `/shared/<plugin id>.<point>/<specifier>.js` file of each shared module of a point that has a granted item of another plugin, whether the requester provides the point or contributes to it. An item is granted when its provider is installed and enabled, the point declares a `version`, and the item's `range` contains that version. An undeclared point, a point without a version, a disabled or missing provider and an out-of-range item grant nothing; a malformed declaration is an error that names it. Red: the Go and Rust tests of the case failed on a stub that returned an empty list, with the assertions recorded in F212.5-3. Green: the same tests pass. The core root that serves these files is connected in F212.5-6.

- F150.2.1: the native library has an event ring (`event_ring.h`): a bounded lock-free ring that many producer threads push variable-length events into without a lock, an allocation or a system call, and that one consumer drains; a full ring or an event larger than half of it returns false and counts the lost events and bytes. `make -C native/darwin benchmark` measures a push (about 80 to 100 ns on the calling thread) against the present text record (about 1.1 microseconds, with a worst case in the tens to hundreds of microseconds).

It moved every shown control except the one directly before the card tools with `insertBefore`, which takes the control out of the document first, and WebKit sends no `click` for a press whose node left the document; the eleventh full window run recorded on Wails a header click that did not open a folded left sidebar because the draw of the preceding fold ran between the press and the release. The rule is stated in the exposure specification. - F62: the Wails persistent transport harness closes the connection that echoed an `open` request instead of the first two connections it accepted, so each host loses its first connection and receives a connection event also when one host's revived connection reaches the service before the other host's first connection. `TestPersistentTransportHarnessEndpointAuthConcurrentReconnectAndCloseAck` gained the subtest `second opens after the first reconnected`, which failed with `no connection event; the test stalled` before the change. The host code and the Tauri harness are unchanged. Validated on macOS 26.6.2 arm64 with the Wails host test package.
- F63: after a refused cleanup probe (`kill(-pgid, 0)` answering EPERM) the command supervisor reads the group's members from the process table (`ps -A -o pid=,pgid=,stat=`), records them in the `verify` cleanup observation, and counts the group as cleaned when no listed member runs; a running member keeps the EPERM failure. macOS answers EPERM for a group whose members have all exited and wait as zombies for their parent, which here was launchd for a descendant whose parent had already exited, and `forwards CLI SIGTERM to command cancellation and cleanup` failed once that way under load. The supervisor tests judge an ended descendant by its process state, because `kill(pid, 0)` succeeds for a zombie. The new test `counts a process group that holds only zombies as gone after a denied probe` failed before the change and passes after it.
- F59: both hosts create owner-only files and directories only through platform operations; Darwin implements them in `platform/darwin/private_files.*` with modes 0700 and 0600, and Windows returns `<operation> is not implemented on windows`. Go gained `CreatePrivateDirectories`, `AppendPrivateFile`, `CreatePrivateFile`, `WritePrivateFile`, `SecureServiceDirectory` and `PrivateDirectory`, and Rust gained `create_private_file`, which creates a file that must not exist, and `write_private_file`, which replaces the contents of a file. The Go log, configuration, settings, process lock, clipboard, service, performance and diagnostic sites no longer set `os` permission modes, which compile on Windows without giving owner-only access. The Tauri process lock had the umask mode 0644 and now has mode 0600, as in Wails; the Tauri services, clipboard, settings, endpoint record and performance logs directories, the performance switch, service flags and output, the WebKit child record and the diagnostic fixture settings are now owner-only, as in Wails. New contract cases `platform.private.creates-owner-only-directories`, `platform.private.appends-owner-only-file`, `platform.private.creates-new-owner-only-file`, `platform.private.writes-owner-only-file`, `performance.trace.owner-only-files`, `webkit-children.record.owner-only` and `endpoint.process.lock-mode-0600`; the last three failed on Tauri before the change. Validated on macOS 26.6.2 arm64 with both host suites and `make windows-build-check`.
- F43: the page draws the DOM of a prepared layout in the callback of the next animation frame after its native preparation answers (`drawPrepared` and `animationFrame(work)` in `packages/workbench/layout-queue.js`); it drew in the microtask checkpoint that resolved the preparation, which can be the checkpoint of a ResizeObserver callback, and the tenth full window run recorded the switch to the library clearing the plane inside an observation round of the files tree observer, which WebKit reported as `ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications.` A layout epoch change before that frame cancels the draw. [Native surfaces](docs/spec/native-surfaces.md) states the rule. The new workbench test `a prepared draw runs at the next animation frame when its preparation is answered inside an observation round` failed before the change and passes after it.
- F60: when a surface is removed, the workbench detaches the regions of its module's compositions before it calls the module's `dispose` (`disposeModule` in `packages/workbench/surface-modules.js`). The terminal and shell modules end their sidecar session in `dispose` before they detach their region, and the supplier releases its transfer images when the session ends, so a frame that it had sent before was presented on a region that was still attached and failed with `error: image present: … reason=notFound`, as in the tenth full window run on Tauri; such a frame is now answered `stale` for a detached region. Both hosts already handled the case the same way, so no host changed. [Plugins](docs/spec/plugins.md#surface-ownership) states the order. Red: `removing a surface detaches its regions before the module ends its sidecar session` failed with the order `session close`, `imageDetach view`; Green: it and the 297 workbench tests pass.

- F41: the window check `late-reply.test.mjs` (`a surface reply that arrives after its surface closed is discarded as an observation`) sends `core.surface.hit` to a new browser tab whose replies the page holds, closes the tab while the reply is held, and requires that the request ends with 1003, that the application log holds the observation `exposure reply <id> of removed surface "<surface>" arrived after its request ended` for that tab, and that no `error: ` line was written. - F50: `core.tab.close` answers after the tab close has disposed the surface and its draw has removed the slot; the handler did not return the close, so the command answered during the disposal and a following command's settled wait read the disposed surface's slot and logged `exposure settled failed: surface … is not mounted`. The settled wait of a core command now waits for the newest layout through `wait()` of the layout queue, which waits again while a newer layout was scheduled; it awaited the layout of its start once, and a layout that a newer one replaces ends without a draw. [Exposure](docs/spec/exposure.md#registration) states the rule. New workbench tests `core.tab.close answers after the tab close and its draw`, `the wait for the drawn layout continues through a layout that a newer layout replaces` and `the wait for the drawn layout fails with the failure of the newest layout` failed before the change and pass after it.
- F35.1: before it answers a page's start document, each host sets the window title bar to the first-row height of the common `textSize`, so the first draw of a window at a frame factor other than 1 no longer shows its row under the 40pt title bar of window creation; `textSize` is common-only in both hosts and the page. A switch to the library is a prepared layout that writes the current frame factor, because the switch cancels a prepared draw that may have been the one writing a new factor. A preparation that fails after it set the title bar sets the earlier height again before it cancels.
- F35.1: the window title bar height joins the layout transaction. Each surface preparation (`syncSurfaces`) carries `titlebar`, the first-row height of the draw that follows it, and both hosts set the title bar after they begin the window's transaction and before they place the surfaces, so the row and the window buttons change in the same presented frame; the preparation answers the window's `chrome`, and verification W compares the row with the `chrome` of the last presented preparation. A frame factor change is now drawn by a prepared layout that writes the factor into the document; before, the setting wrote it at once and the page requested the title bar after the draw with `windowTitlebar`, which is removed with `packages/workbench/titlebar.js`. In full screen the hosts leave the title bar unchanged instead of failing, and the page prepares its row again when a `windowControls` answer shows a title bar that differs from it.
- F35.1: the native check `window_titlebar_layout_test` records a window while it sets the title bar height inside an open layout transaction and fails when a recorded frame shows the window buttons at the new place before `surfaceLayoutCommit` or not after it; on macOS 26.6.2 the buttons moved only with the commit.
- F46: both hosts declare the status `host.buttons` `{mask}`, the `NSEvent.pressedMouseButtons` mask that the 1007 refusal reads; `native/darwin` reads it at every mouse button press and release that AppKit delivers to the application or, through a global event monitor, to another application, and the hosts notify watchers when it changes. The window-check harness ends a press that a check left open by waiting through `status.watch` until `host.buttons` reports mask 0 and then requiring the release to be delivered; before, it sent the release again while a person still held the button, the release was refused again, and every later pointer check of that host failed with 1008.
- F48: the Tauri `host.windows` reads the close state, title and focus of every window in one main-thread step; it read the close state on the endpoint thread and queried each window in separate main-thread round trips, so a close that the main thread processed in between failed the list with `runtime error: failed to receive message from webview`. The new contract case `exposure.windows.listed-in-one-main-thread-step` reproduced the failure with a close queued on a test main thread before the change and passes after it; the Wails list needs no change.
- F49: removing a project from the registry, by its project tab or by `core.library.remove` in another window, ends it in the window that shows it as closing its tab does: that window reads the removal from the registry change notification, disposes the surface modules of the project's tabs before it ends their sidecar sessions, and opens its first remaining project or shows the library as a window without a project. The window kept the removed project's surface modules and terminal sessions and did not open its next project tab.
- F51: each host request that uses the native window reads it in the main-thread step that passes it to native code. The Tauri `host.window`, `host.window.fullscreen`, `host.window.move`, `host.hit`, `input.pointer`, `input.key`, surface press watch and surface layout steps read the NSWindow in one main-thread step and used it in a later one; tauri-runtime-wry closes the NSWindow and tao releases it in the main-thread pass that accepts a close, before `Destroyed`, so a close in between passed a closed and possibly freed window to native code. The Wails host read the window in the step that uses it but passed the nil of a destroyed window to native code. On both hosts a window that closed before that step now fails the request with 1003 `window "<name>" does not exist` and reaches no native code, and a `host.window` change of it notifies nothing; the Tauri surface press after `input.pointer` no longer hit-tests AppKit views on the endpoint thread, and the Tauri unknown-window message quotes the name as Wails does. The new contract case `window-close.native-window.used-in-reading-step` failed before the change on both hosts and passes after it.
- F47: the hosts write every failure as an error line `error: <where>: <text>`, the form of the page, through `LogError` (Go), `log_error` (Rust) and the native `sp_log_error`, with the same text on both hosts at a shared site, so a window check sees host failures; Wails framework errors take the same path. A host line without `error: ` is an observation that states the expected state, such as `<result> arrived after its request ended`; a late result that carries a failure is now written as an error. The workbench wrote `exposure settled failed: …`, `exposure: …` and the layout queue failure without `error: ` and now writes them as error lines. The native surface settle line wrote a literal `\n` and joined the next log line to it.
- F35: the page sets the window title bar to the height of its first row through the new `windowTitlebar` host call, so AppKit centres the window buttons in the row at every frame text factor; the hosts set the height with AppKit's `-[NSWindow setTitlebarHeight:]` instead of an empty unified compact toolbar, which fixed the title bar at 40pt, and the row no longer reads its height back from the window, which kept it from shrinking. - F37: a synthetic `input.pointer` press or release that AppKit refuses with a nonzero `NSEvent.pressedMouseButtons` mask returns 1007 with the mask and the frontmost application's bundle identifier and pid, measured in the same main run-loop turn as the refusal, in the same text on both hosts; the message before named neither.
- F43: after a ResizeObserver loop error, the diagnostic recorder reports the DOM changes of the error frame by callback slot: the changes still undelivered at the first callback, the changes of each callback and its microtask checkpoint with the code that created its observer, and the changes after the round until the next animation frame; before, one line held every change from the first callback to the next animation frame.

The plugin-api, workbench, host, `sok` and workspace registry tests reproduce the new contract (Red before the change: `unknown field dependencies`, no installed sidecar declarations, undefined `ManifestSidecars` and `manifest_sidecars`), and root `pnpm test`, `make boundaries`, `make exposure-check`, `make hosts-check` and `make docs-check` pass on macOS 26 (darwin-arm64).
- F28: a window check whose pasteboard differs afterwards names the item, the type and the length and digest of each side.
- F27: the window check of the OSC 9 notification policy fits the bundled applications: it names an undecided notification authorization and checks that the tab policy adds no system notification.
- F24: the window check of a failed terminal presentation waits for the next terminals to present instead of failing while they have not presented yet.
- R2-4-3: `docs/spec/registry.md` specifies the public registry: committed entry files, pull requests by entry owners, an automatic check and merge, and publication of the index on merge.
- R2-9: the applications and `sok` no longer move the 0.0.2 configuration folders or convert `installed.json` format 1; a file of another format fails with its name.
- R2-7-3: `docs/plans/linux-host.md` proposes the Linux host: the framework facts, the Linux mechanism of each host operation group and private API, the vt frame transport, the decisions D1–D8 and the order of implementation.
- R2-7-2: the files sidecar watches directories on Linux with inotify (sidecar-files S8).
- R2-7-1: `sok` runs on Linux with the configuration directory under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `~/.config`; `sok path` reports that Linux has no path entry folder, and the CI workflow runs the `sok` tests on Linux.
- F23: the Go `sok` writes extracted files at mode 0755 or 0644 whatever the process umask is; under the umask 077 it wrote a sidecar executable at mode 0700.
- F14: both applications answer the operating system's quit request (Dock, logout, restart, another program) without an error after their saves; the Wails application answered it with a cancellation, which also stops a logout, and the Tauri application ended without waiting for page saves.
- F21: both hosts accept a persistent service's answer to a close sent before the quit, so the quit still sends `shutdown` and the terminal service ends with the application.
- R2-5-1: core has a CI workflow and a release workflow; a tag publishes the two applications as zip files with the installation guide `docs/operations/install.md`.
- F22: the repeat tool's tests remove `NO_COLOR` from the environment they pass, so an environment with `NO_COLOR` no longer puts a node warning into the output they match.
- R2-6-2: the command `core.plugins.registry` sets the registry index, and a window check installs over https from a test-owned TLS registry and refuses a wrong hash, a revoked version and an unreachable registry.
- R2-6-1: a diagnostic build accepts `--registry-ca PATH`, so a window check can serve a local TLS registry; a release build rejects the argument.
- F20: both applications reject an undeclared argument, a flag without a value and a repeated flag with the same text and status 2; the Tauri application no longer ignores them.
- F15: both hosts report a malformed `process.lock` with the same text, `<path>: invalid process lock`.
- F18, F19: a terminal accepts pointer points in the band where the native region is smaller than its view, and a failed mouse operation answers with its own result, so the page no longer reports `unexpected mouse inputId`.
- R2-4-1: both hosts and `sok` read registry indexes and archives over https with fixed redirect, time and size limits, and the first run sets the default registry of `environment.json` with `pluginsUseRegistry`.
- F17: the startup-timeout tests of both hosts no longer depend on when the silent service starts.
- R2-2-2: the plugin and sidecar repositories declare version 0.0.3, and `@soksak/plugin-api` provides `soksak-engines`, which fails when a plugin's `engines.soksak` is not `^<version>` of the plugin API it builds against.
- F16: `soksak-exposure` and `soksak-engines` run their check when a plugin repository starts them through the linked package; before, they ended without checking.
- R2-2-1: every core declaration is 0.0.3, and the version check also covers the application `Info.plist` versions and the native pkg-config version.
- R2-8: both release applications are `soksak.app` with the bundle identifiers `app.soksak.wails` and `app.soksak.tauri`; development builds use `.dev` identifiers; the first release start moves the former `com.soksak.*` configuration folder once, and `plugins/installed.json` format 2 records installed folders relative to the configuration directory, converting a format 1 file once (R2-8-1).
- G4-3: test evidence records a renamed path with its original path and reads paths that `git status` would quote, so `pnpm test` no longer fails while a rename is staged.
- R2-1: the Go modules, package fields and documented install commands name the `soksak-app` organization (`github.com/soksak-app/core`), the license holder is `soksak`, personal paths are removed from the records, and the plugin specification states the GitHub repository of each sibling folder and the checkout layout.
- G1.4-116: both hosts wait for each visible image region's raster of the prepared size before they commit a continuous layout too, so a divider drag no longer shows a grown region with the previous raster; the drag frame counts did not drop at comparable load.
- G1.4-90-4-2: an image region attached again in the same generation continues its raster revision in both hosts, so the terminal sidecar no longer ignores its configuration and the presentation no longer waits 10 s for a terminal mounted again; both hosts trace their image raster decisions.
- G1.4-90-4-2: the terminal sidecar opens a surface again after a `close` request on a persistent connection (vt S14), which removes the 10 s raster timeouts of the terminal checks; the earlier input-stall diagnosis was measured during a check that stops the service on purpose and is withdrawn.
- G1.4-112: a failed image region call names the call in both hosts, as `<call>: <reason>`; host contract case `images.calls.name-the-call`.
- G1.4-110: the Tauri host refuses a page's status change of a host status as the Wails host does, with `the page cannot change host status <name>`; host contract case `exposure.status-change.refuses-host-name`.
- G1.4-113: a failed project switch is reported once, by the caller that receives the rejection, instead of also as a window error. Red and Green in `packages/workbench/test/projects-switch.test.mjs`; the library and projects window checks pass on both rebuilt hosts.
- G1.4-111: a window check fails when the main page shows an application error that the check did not declare with `expectPageError`, and the main page reports a status change that the host refuses with the status name. Red and Green in `e2e/test/session-cleanup.test.mjs` and `packages/workbench/test/exposure.test.mjs`; the new check found G1.4-113.
- G1.4-105-2, G1.4-105-3: both hosts decode every host call argument with their own decoder and refuse a missing or `null` required field, a value of another JSON type, a number outside an integer field's range and a fixed-length array of another length with the same text, `argument <path> <problem>`; the Wails host no longer turns a missing field into its zero value, and the two hosts' argument types were aligned field by field. Red through each framework's decode path, recorded after the change; Green in the Go and Rust host tests, the host contract check and 119 window checks on both rebuilt hosts.
- G1.4-109: the Wails host runs `ImageCaret` and `ImageText` sent from a surface page through the native bridge with their own argument lists; before, both failed with `<call> expects 1 arguments`. `TestNativeImageCallsDecodeTheirOwnArguments` failed before the change and passes after it.
- G1.4-102: `make page-memory` measures the main page process of a running application, by default a release build, at start, after an idle time and after reloads; the release measurement shows no idle growth, and after G1.4-107 a reload leaves no previous page process.
- G1.4-107: a reload or page change of the main page opens the new document in a new WebContent process and ends the previous one, so the main page no longer keeps every replaced document until memory pressure; the page footprint stays flat over 20 reloads.
- G1.4-90-4-2: the main page numbers every surface composition placement of a document with one increasing revision, so a surface mounted again in the same document is no longer refused with `stale composition revision 1`.
- G1.4-105-1: the Wails host refuses `null` in a numeric field of a host call argument instead of reading it as 0, and refuses a workspace `move` without `delta` with `move delta is missing`, as the Tauri host does.
- G1.4-105: the main page refuses a host call whose argument contains NaN or Infinity before sending it, with one `TypeError` on both hosts, because JSON would send the number as `null` and the hosts decode `null` differently.
- G1.4-106: the Tauri host places the window overlays before it begins a surface layout, as the Wails host does, and cancels a begun layout when a later step or the image raster refresh fails, so a failed surface sync no longer leaves the window's layout transaction open.
- G1.4-101: the window check `window-release.test.mjs` also requires the web content process of each closed project window to exit, waiting through the new diagnostic `diagnostics.process.exit`, which answers when the kernel reports the process's exit.
- G1.4-101-1: `diagnostics.native.objects` accepts `equal` and replies when the counts reach it, draining the autorelease pool with a posted event each time the main run loop is about to wait, because AppKit keeps a closed window until its close animation ends and releases an object autoreleased during a pool drain at the next drain; `window-release.test.mjs` waits this way and passes on both hosts with the tao pin.
- G1.4-101-1: diagnostic builds of both hosts report the live window compositions, surface hosts, and input registrations of the shared macOS library through `diagnostics.native.objects`, counted after the application has handled an event, and the window check `window-release.test.mjs` requires four closed project windows to leave these counts unchanged.
- G1.4-104: the Wails host refuses a surface sync request with an invalid surface rectangle instead of ending with `fatal error: sync: unlock of unlocked mutex`, and both hosts check every rectangle of the request before the layout begins, so a refused window overlay no longer leaves a begun layout in the Tauri host.
- G1.4-101-1: the Tauri host uses tao 0.37.1 with the upstream tao fix that releases closed windows, so a closed window and its webview are released.
- G1.4-101: closing a window closes the document regions, image regions, and logical surfaces of the window in both hosts, a webview's input registration ends when the webview is released, and the file drop receiver is freed with its drop view, so a closed window no longer keeps its main webview, document webviews, and their web content processes.
- G1.4-103: Wails is v3.0.0-beta.27 and Tauri is the released 2.12.1 with wry 0.57.0 and tao 0.37.1 from crates.io, without the git pin; the Wails builds offer the Web Inspector through Safari instead of inside the window.
- G1.4-100: turning the performance trace off stops a persistent sidecar's events on connections accepted while it was on.
- G1.4-90-4-1: the Wails host handles a webview's document commit before the messages that the webview sent after it.
- G1.4-99: the Wails host closes a sidecar's output pipe when it stops reading it, so a sidecar that still writes while stopping ends without the force-kill, as in the Tauri host.
- G1.4-98: a retain of the Wails host that a stop interrupts fails with "sidecars are stopped" instead of sending to a closed channel, and a full outbox fails the retain at once, as in the Tauri host.
- G1.4-94: a main-page command whose handler throws no longer leaves a reply timer that logs `did not reply within 10000ms` ten seconds later.
- G1.4-97: the Wails host no longer panics when a window closes while the application stops its sidecars; stopping removes the sidecars from the running set first, as in the Tauri host.
- G1.4-87: a sidebar set line uses the width beside its buttons, and Korean text wraps at spaces instead of between syllables.
- G1.4-87: the settings window draws each setting form with one control: a switch, a select box for every choice, the theme swatches, a slider, or a text field; choices are no longer rows of buttons, and `core.settings-modal` reports the options of each select box.
- G1.4-86: plugins are installed, updated, removed, enabled and disabled on the 플러그인 page of the library, which shows each plugin's description, versions and sidecars; the settings window keeps only the settings of loaded plugins and opens that page with 플러그인 관리.
- G1.4-96: a window check confirms that the settings modal is on screen at the presented time once the window reports it shown, and the example verification states that wait for modal captures.
- G1.4-95: a window check prints each failed cleanup step as a diagnostic, so a cleanup failure is visible when the check itself failed.
- G1.4-93: the test runner leaves a forced kill that macOS refuses with EPERM to its cleanup check instead of failing a timed-out run.
- G1.4-85: the specification states which control takes a press where a folded card sidebar strip meets a card divider, and a window check measures it.
- G1.4-84: a folded card sidebar shows three dots, distinct from the bar grip of a card divider.
- G1.4-83: the card header has a fold and open control for each sidebar the card shows.
- G1.4-82: the status line of a window sidebar ends in a fold control that turns the sidebar off.
- G1.4-81: the content footer of a card shows the footer text that the active tab's plugin reports: the terminal's working directory and the address of the link under the pointer in a browser document.
- G1.4-80: card sidebars end in their own status line, and the content footer of a card spans only its content column.
- G1.4-90-7: a window in full screen answers `windowControls` with title bar row 0 instead of an error.
- G1.4-90-5: both hosts log a replaced image frame as invalidated with the same text and log another presentation failure with the current frame state.
- G1.4-90-3: a delegated root no longer runs the command of an element connected with `bind` a second time, so Enter in the browser address field navigates once.
- G1.4-90-2: a sidebar section that follows a core status mounts after a reload, because the core statuses are registered before the first section mounts.
- G1.4-90-1: a reload request makes a ready page reload itself after its host calls are answered, so Wails no longer loses a host reply on each reload.
- G1.4-88: a pointer down while a synthetic press of that button is open in the window returns 1008, and a check session releases every press it left open.
- G1.4-92: the documentation check reads a committed checklist larger than 1 MiB.
- G1.4-79: the terminal runtime specification states that a narrowing reflow uses the empty rows below the cursor before it moves rows into the history.
- G1.4-76: both hosts keep the application log in `logs/application.log` under the configuration directory, persistent services write theirs to `logs/<executable-name>.log`, and a log of 10 MB or more moves to `.1` when it is opened.
- G1.4-77: a settings change keeps the scroll position of the settings window; the window reports `scroll` in `core.settings-modal`.
- G1.4-75: reading the settings deletes a stored link to a set that no longer exists, saves the result and logs it, instead of failing to load the settings.
- G1.4-74: a first run without a plugin registry shows why no plugin was installed and how to set the registry.
- G1.4-73: window checks register cleanup with the session, compare settings rows with the declared keys, judge WebView churn by the window documents, measure the wheel factor, and load a local document instead of an external site.
- G1.4-72: the terminal runtime specification defines the per-side terminal padding settings, and a window check measures the inset grid and the padding color.
- G1.4-63-1: sidecars answer every `closed` with `{surface, closed: true[, error]}`; both hosts list unanswered closes in the `host.sidecars` status, log failed closes, and the PTY reap check waits on that status.
- G1.4-70: both hosts wait at most 30 s for a new persistent service's ready line and 5 s for its hello reply, end and reap a service that never becomes ready, and report the same error texts.
- G1.4-68: both hosts start a sidecar with the registry lock released, so a persistent service start no longer delays sends to other sidecars; stop waits for starts in progress.
- G1.4-63: the PTY reap check waits up to 10 s for the shells to end after the terminal surfaces close and reports the close and end times, instead of reading the process list once.

- G1.4-55: the slow-sidecar send tests of both hosts start the fast sidecar before they time a send to it, so the 50 ms limit no longer includes the process start.

- G1.4-64-1-5: both hosts create windows hidden and show them transparent until the main webview's first load has ended and the next presentation has completed, so a new window and the first window at startup open with their first screen instead of an empty window; the endpoint specification lists the `display` option of `diagnostics.capture.start`.

- G1.4-64-1-2: the main page starts with its start document (`/start.json` on Wails, `soksak://localhost/start.json` on Tauri) that carries the workspace snapshot and the window controls; answering it performs the page-start cleanup and replaces the `pageStarted` call, and each runtime provides `runtime/start.js`.
- G1.4-64-1-2: both hosts serve each enabled plugin's manifest in `/installed-plugins.json`, and the workbench registers `exposure.json`, `environment.json` and the installed plugins from JSON modules without requesting each `plugin.json`.
- G1.4-64-1-4: `webview_process_test` reproduces WebKit's `querySelectorAll` result cache keeping a replaced document after reload; both hosts add `diagnostics.page.collect`, and the private native API inventory records the cause and the collection request.
- G1.4-64-1: the surface composition specification no longer states that a reload shows the window background; an empty window during a reload is a defect.
- G1.4-64: a window check measures that a library visit shows no empty frame; the surface composition specification states that a reload shows the window background until the new page draws.
- G1.4-62-1: a drawn commit that repeats the prepared placement writes the paint clip of that placement.
- G1.4-61: a main-page reload hides the native surfaces before the page disappears on both hosts.
- G1.4-62: the page paint clip keeps the holes of the newest placement when an older placement answer arrives later.
- G1.4-58-1: the orientation check reads which of top and bottom opened.
- G1.4-59: the empty-state check waits for the address field focus before it types.
- G1.4-58: a folded card sidebar opens by click or drag whenever it fits; sides that do not fit together are shown smaller, and the card status line names a side folded for lack of space.
- G1.4-56: a folded card sidebar shows a short grip in the divider grip colours instead of a line along the side or a tick across it.
- G1.4-57: the placement check links a terminal card sidebar before it toggles it, because the default layout has none.
- G1.4-54: the gesture check looks for a state from the display of the previous state, because the reported display time can follow the first display, and its failure message lists the frame times around a missed state.
